*Learn-the-tool track · Lab 3 of 3.*

The forward map answers "how much do these share?" in nats.  You will estimate
mutual information and check it against a case with a known answer.

---

## 1 · The Estimator on Three Shapes

```{python}
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
n = 3000
indep = (rng.normal(size=n), rng.normal(size=n))
lin = rng.multivariate_normal([0, 0], [[1, 0.7], [0.7, 1]], size=n)
s = rng.normal(size=n); curve = (s, s**2 + 0.3 * rng.normal(size=n))

shapes = [("independent", indep),
          ("linear ρ=0.7", (lin[:, 0], lin[:, 1])),
          ("U-shape (curved)", curve)]
for name, (xx, yy) in shapes:
    print(f"{name:<18} MI ≈ {mutual_information_xy(xx, yy):.3f} nats")
```

See the data behind those numbers — the same scatter, three different
dependencies:

```{python}
#| label: fig-tool3-shapes
#| fig-cap: "The three pairs whose MI is reported above. MI is ~0 for the independent cloud and lights up for both the linear tilt and the curve (which a correlation would miss)."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3.8))
for ax, (name, (xx, yy)) in zip(axes, shapes):
    ax.scatter(xx, yy, s=8, c=COOL, alpha=0.3, edgecolors="none")
    ax.set_title(f"{name}\nMI ≈ {mutual_information_xy(xx, yy):.2f} nats", fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Independent ≈ a small finite-sample floor; both dependent shapes light up —
including the curve a correlation would miss.

---

## 2 · Validate Against the Gaussian Closed Form

For a Gaussian pair, $I = -\tfrac12 \ln(1-\rho^2)$.

```{python}
#| label: fig-tool3-validate
#| fig-cap: "Estimated vs exact mutual information across correlations."
rhos = np.linspace(0, 0.9, 10)
truth = [-0.5 * np.log(1 - r**2) for r in rhos]
est = []
for r in rhos:
    xy = rng.multivariate_normal([0, 0], [[1, r], [r, 1]], size=4000)
    est.append(mutual_information_xy(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], bins=24))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.8, 4.2))
ax.plot(rhos, truth, c=INK, lw=2.4, label="exact")
ax.plot(rhos, est, "o", c=COOL, label="estimate")
ax.set_xlabel("ρ"); ax.set_ylabel("MI (nats)")
ax.legend(fontsize=9, frameon=False); despine(ax)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to Look for
The estimate tracks the truth but sits a touch high at ρ=0 — the finite-sample
**bias floor** of any histogram MI.  Always compare a measured MI to the floor on
shuffled data, never to zero.
:::
